units.en: With ⟦0⟧, the Raj has a sprawling focus tree that can be very powerful, but is also full of "trap" options that appear beneficial on paper but end up being detrimental in practice. Examples of these "trap" options include ⟦1⟧ (whose long completion time, increased ⟦2⟧ target, and lack of meaningful unlocks end up making the one ⟦3⟧ and pitiful ⟦4⟧ increase it provides not worth it), ⟦5⟧ (whose ⟦6⟧ do not actually provide any meaningful benefits after accounting for the misleading way the game handles ⟦7⟧), and ⟦8⟧ (which does not provide any real benefits over sticking to ⟦9⟧ at peace-time and ⟦10⟧ at wartime even if it can be taken early thanks to the Axis powers generating a lot of early World Tension). It can also be very easy to inadvertently sabotage Raj's build by taking certain focuses too early, e.g., taking ⟦11⟧ before it gives at least 2 ⟦12⟧ or taking military factory focuses too early and therefore wasting their size increase effects for key ⟦13⟧ on smaller sizes that would require fewer funds to increase normally, thus unnecessarily delaying the incredibly powerful ⟦14⟧. It is therefore important to prioritize: focus on economy- and research-related focuses early, pivot to military factory-related focuses afterwards, and then focus on picking up the numerous stats bonuses that Raj has in their new focus tree, including from ⟦15⟧, ⟦16⟧, ⟦17⟧, ⟦18⟧, and ⟦19⟧ (the bonuses of which are contained in an event that fires immediately after its completion). Special attention should also be paid to ⟦20⟧, as its research bonuses can be used to get earlier access to critical infantry weapon technologies, usually either ⟦21⟧ or ⟦22⟧ depending on who else is rushing those technologies on the Allies. Acquiring ⟦23⟧ status and, eventually, freedom is still helpful and can be done with the same ⟦24⟧ ⟦25⟧ tricks as without the DLC, but is not as vital to get done as early as possible as it is without the DLC. Once all stat bonuses have been acquired, it is likely a good idea to pick up as many focuses that will prevent the spread of famine. The Bengal Famine is especially devastating with ⟦26⟧, and reaching 100% famine spread prevention as early as possible is vital to making sure it only lasts 6-10 months instead of the years that it can otherwise last. Remember to have ⟦27⟧ researched before the famine starts to be able to immediately use the decision unlocked by ⟦28⟧.
For the People, By the People

Regardless of DLCs, Raj has to deal with limited research slots for most of the game, as well as potential ⟦0⟧ issues. The upside is that the land fronts they are expected to have with ⟦1⟧ tend to be quite rugged, filled with ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ provinces (though perhaps unexpectedly, no ⟦5⟧ provinces outside of a handful in Burma). For these reasons, it is usually a good idea to take the Mass Mobilization side of the ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, to lean heavily into land units with terrain bonuses in these provinces like ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, and ⟦10⟧, and to try to get early access to both ⟦11⟧ and ⟦12⟧ to make the ⟦13⟧ and ⟦14⟧ units fielded in these provinces as powerful as they can be. Technology choices should be triaged because of the low research slot count, as Raj simply cannot afford to pick up useful but otherwise luxury options like ⟦15⟧ or ⟦16⟧ without denying themselves timely access to other, more critical technologies. If ⟦17⟧ issues can be overcome, e.g., through reducing the impact of Agrarian Society earlier and/or more or saving up a lot of ⟦18⟧ to switch to ⟦19⟧, the Infiltration side of ⟦20⟧ or the Shock and Awe side of ⟦21⟧ can also work for ⟦22⟧ choices, though care should be taken to deploy units with highly upgraded ⟦23⟧ to avoid ⟦24⟧. It is also important to make sure Raj's few ports are fully garrisonned against any ⟦25⟧ that ⟦26⟧ might attempt once they stop making progress over land.
This guide assumes the ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are ⟦2⟧ while ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ remain ⟦5⟧.

With so few ⟦0⟧ and many ⟦1⟧, trade is important for the Raj in the early game for gaining more civilian industrial points, allowing India to build up its industry to rival that of some of the less industrialized great powers. However, as long as the Raj remains a ⟦2⟧ of the ⟦3⟧, it cannot remove risk of famine, and until it becomes independent, it cannot take advantage of its large manpower and cannot access 2 of its 5 research slots. Therefore, quickly gaining ⟦4⟧ status and independence should be top priorities of the player.

The most efficient way to gain the autonomy needed for dominion and independence is war contribution and lend-leasing to the ⟦0⟧. Both war contribution and lend-lease material can be gained very early in the war through a naval invasion of Italy originating from southern ⟦1⟧ (before ⟦2⟧ is invaded by ⟦3⟧) and then capitulation of ⟦4⟧. In single-player, ⟦5⟧ really is the “soft underbelly of Europe”. The captured war materials can then be shipped to the ⟦6⟧ to increase autonomy. The player must finish ⟦7⟧ within 300 days of the start of WWII in order assure the Bengal Famine is avoided. A rapid capitulation of ⟦8⟧ has the additional advantage of tipping the balance of power between Allies and Axis enough that ⟦9⟧ can hold off the German invasion.

Capturing factories from the Axis means that the British investment focuses are not worth it for the player in single-player, since these focuses greatly slow down independence and the rewards from these focuses are a pittance compared to what can be captured (also the railroad construction bonus is lost on independence). ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are also not worth it (unless one is aiming for the “Our Words Are Backed With Nuclear Weapons” achievement). Remember that autonomy is being lost passively for India every day, meaning each extra focus has an additional autonomy cost. ⟦2⟧ must be taken to get dominion status, despite its bad effects. ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ can be released as puppets when the player gets a notification of unrest in the northwest and northeast in order to avoid civil war.

An AI ⟦0⟧ pursuing a Southern Expansion strategy will become a threat to India around 1942 or so (assuming the war in Europe has not already been won). However, India is at the limit of ⟦1⟧’s naval reach and is defended by mountain and jungle terrain so not many forces are needed to stop ⟦2⟧ (a few ships in the Bay of Bengal can prevent naval invasion). Just make sure your defensive lines are supplied and entrenched.

The British Raj will be behind technologically until independence so pick one or two aspects of your military (such as the air force) to do very well and get ahead-of-time to compensate for weaknesses elsewhere. India remains part of Commonwealth Tech Sharing with full bonuses even after independence so its research could very well eventually become ⟦0⟧ than any other country's (besides the ⟦1⟧) once all 5 research slots are unlocked. Further boosts can be picked up by stealing blueprints while getting the "Spies Trade" achievement.
Take as much as possible in peace negotiations to propel India to major power status and perhaps even leadership of the Allied faction.
